verses.text: When people have a quarrel, they must take it to court, and the judges will decide the case. They must declare the innocent person right and the guilty person wrong.
If the guilty person deserves to be beaten, the judge must make him lie down and have him beaten in front of him, with the number of lashes his crime deserves.
The judge may not give more than forty lashes. If he gives more than that, your fellow Israelite would be shamed in front of you.
Do not cover an ox's mouth to stop it eating while it is treading out the grain.

Suppose brothers are living together, and one of them dies without a son. His widow must not marry someone outside the family. Her husband's brother must marry her and do his duty as a brother-in-law.
The first son she has will carry on the name of the dead brother, so that his name will not be wiped out from Israel.

But if the man does not want to marry his brother's widow, she must go to the town leaders at the gate and say, "My husband's brother refuses to carry on his brother's name in Israel. He will not do his duty as a brother-in-law to me."
Then the leaders of his town will call for him and talk to him. If he still says, "I do not want to marry her,"

his brother's widow must go up to him in front of the leaders, pull one of his sandals off his foot, and spit in his face. She will say, "This is what happens to the man who will not build up his brother's family."
From then on his family will be known in Israel as "the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off."
If two men are fighting, and the wife of one of them comes to rescue her husband from the man hitting him, and she reaches out and grabs the other man by his private parts,
you must cut off her hand. Do not feel sorry for her.
Do not carry two different weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.
Do not keep two different measures in your house, one large and one small.
Use weights and measures that are accurate and honest, so that you will live a long time in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
For the LORD your God hates anyone who does such things, anyone who is dishonest.
Remember what the Amalekites did to you on your journey after you left Egypt.
When you were tired and worn out, they met you on the road and attacked everyone who was weak and lagging behind. They had no fear of God.
When the LORD your God gives you rest from all the enemies around you in the land he is giving you to own as your share, you must wipe out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget!
